input.rationale: Measuring the one consequence the asserted defect had not yet witnessed: what each trigger actually does once the node's store sits below its snapshot index. The harness drives a real single-node cluster with TrailingLogs=0 and a high SnapshotThreshold to the emptied state, records store last index, snapshot index, applied index, stored-snapshot count and shouldSnapshot, then calls the production takeSnapshot twice and records the same operands after each call. Native construction feedback with these fixed inputs gave: emptied state store_last=0, snapshot_index=3, applied=3, stored snapshots=1, should_snapshot=true; then two successful takeSnapshot calls that each created another snapshot at the unchanged index 3 while applied stayed 3, taking the stored count to 3. That is the redundant work the claim predicts, repeatable rather than a one-off. The same run also exposed a store-specific detail worth recording: after the second compaction the InmemStore reported store_last=18446744073709551615, so the trigger fired there through a wrapped store index rather than a delta subtraction; the generic emptied-store reading is the first sample, and I am noting the artifact so it is not folded into the claim. This submission records the fixed experiment for controller execution; the measured interpretation is left for the retained receipt.

scope.description: One process, one real single-node cluster with TrailingLogs=0, SnapshotThreshold=10000 and SnapshotInterval=1h. After the node becomes leader one command is applied and a user Snapshot() is run, then store last index, snapshot index, applied index, stored-snapshot count and shouldSnapshot are recorded. The production takeSnapshot is then invoked twice, and after each invocation the same operands are recorded together with the returned snapshot-id presence and any error.

experiment.prefix: inmemConfig supplies the defaults; TrailingLogs=0 makes the compaction triggered by the user snapshot trim up to the snapshot index and the large threshold makes the control verdict false before that. MakeCluster(1, t, conf) starts the real node over InmemTransport with InmemStore for logs and stable state; the test waits for Leader before applying so the apply is accepted. takeSnapshot is the package-internal production routine that runSnapshots calls on its own timer, so invoking it directly removes the wait on SnapshotInterval while still exercising the production snapshot, compaction and configuration-read paths and the FSM's Snapshot call; no production logic is modified and all operands are package-internal reads of the runtime object plus the snapshot store's List().

scope.description: Two-voter in-process cluster over InmemTransport, plus one real unbootstrapped raft instance merged into the same network; call AddVoter for the new server on the current leader, record the future result and index, then sample each node's reported configuration every 100ms for 3s.

basis.prefix: MakeCluster(2) starts a bootstrapped pair and waits for a leader; MakeClusterNoBootstrap(1) creates the new node with empty log and no configuration; Merge and FullyConnect wire the transports so the new node is reachable but has an empty log. The leader calls AddVoter(newID, newAddr, 0, 0) with prevIndex 0. Observations are the AddVoter future result/index and, per node, num_servers/num_voters/has_new_member sampled from the node's locally reported configuration, emitted as CA_EVENT JSON.

scope.description: One process: bootstrapped two-Voter cluster (quorum 2) plus one real Nonvoter added with AddNonvoter while fully connected, then two withheld-side cases in the same execution. Case A withholds the Nonvoter's transport and applies one command; case B reconnects everyone, withholds a Voter's transport and applies one command. Each case emits the leader's last log index, the leader's commit index and the nonvoter's last log index, plus whether the apply future completed inside an 800ms window and its error.

basis.prefix: MakeCluster(2) bootstraps the two Voters and waits for a leader; MakeClusterNoBootstrap(1) creates the Nonvoter with an empty log; Merge plus FullyConnect wire all three transports so the Nonvoter is reachable and can store entries. The leader calls AddNonvoter(id, address, 0, 0) and the test waits 300ms so the nonvoting configuration is committed and the Nonvoter's log has caught up (baseline records leader_last_index=3, nonvoter_last_index=3). Isolation uses the cluster's transport-level Disconnect on the withheld node's address, which removes it in both directions without modifying production logic; FullyConnect restores it. Observability uses the package-internal getLastIndex/getCommitIndex accessors on the real raft objects, so the operands are the runtime state of the objects under test rather than a derived label.

scope.description: One process, three real raft instances (MakeCluster(3)) plus one restart. A RequestVote RPC is sent from one node's transport into the target node's consumer for candidate A in term target.getCurrentTerm()+5 with LastLogIndex/LastLogTerm taken from the target's own last entry so the log-up-to-date rule grants, and LeadershipTransfer=true so the known-leader rule does not decide the outcome. The target's granted flag and its durable LastVoteTerm/LastVoteCand keys are sampled before and after restarting the target over the same stores, followed by three further RPCs (same candidate same term, different candidate same term, different candidate older term).

basis.prefix: MakeCluster(3) bootstraps three Voters over InmemTransport and waits for a leader, so both candidate IDs are Voters in the target's latest configuration and the cluster has a known leader. The target is raft 2 and the sender transport is raft 0's. Every request sets RPCHeader{ProtocolVersion:3, ID: candidateID, Addr: encoded candidate} so the handler resolves the candidate from the header exactly as a real peer would. The restart is performed by shutting the target down (Shutdown().Error() waits for its routines) and calling NewRaft with a copy of the cluster Config whose LocalID is the target's, reusing the same InmemStore for both LogStore and StableStore, the same MockFSM, the same snapshot store and the same transport; no production logic is modified and no source is edited.

scope.description: One process: three real raft instances are bootstrapped (MakeCluster(3)) and then the target is isolated from the other two with the cluster's transport-level Disconnect. A dedicated InmemTransport is connected only to the target's transport and is used for every probe. A RequestVote for candidate A in term target.getCurrentTerm()+5 is delivered into the target's consumer and the granted flag plus the durable LastVoteTerm/LastVoteCand keys are recorded. The target is then shut down and rebuilt over the same log/stable/snapshot stores, FSM and transport; immediately afterwards the restored currentTerm and durable vote keys are recorded with an applicability flag, and three probes are issued inside the election-timer window: the same candidate in the same term, a different candidate in the same term, and a different candidate in an older term.

basis.prefix: MakeCluster(3) bootstraps three Voters over InmemTransport and waits for a leader, so both candidate IDs are Voters in the target's latest configuration; the target is raft 2, and the candidate IDs/addresses come from rafts 1 and 0. Isolation uses cluster.Disconnect on the target's address, which removes the target from every other transport's peer map and disconnects the target from them, without editing production source. Delivery is preserved because the probe transport is connected to the target's transport separately, so the target still receives RPCs while its real peers cannot advance its term. Every request sets RPCHeader{ProtocolVersion:3, ID: candidateID, Addr: encoded candidate} and takes LastLogIndex/LastLogTerm from the target's own last entry so the log-up-to-date rule grants, with LeadershipTransfer=true so the known-leader rule does not decide the outcome. After the restart the probes run with no sleep so they precede the fresh node's first heartbeat-timeout election; the harness emits restored currentTerm against the probe term and the durable vote term so applicability is checkable from the receipt alone.

experiments.revision_reason: The previous execution could not exercise the same-term duplicate rule: the target remained a live voter whose real peers advanced its term past the probe term after it accepted a future-term vote, so all post-restart probes were decided by the older-term rule. This revision isolates the target from its peers and probes immediately after the restart within the election-timer window.

scope.description: One process, one real single-node cluster with TrailingLogs=0, SnapshotThreshold=10000 and SnapshotInterval=1h. After the node becomes leader two commands are applied, then shouldSnapshot(), the log store's LastIndex, the cached snapshot index and the commit index are recorded (control). A user-triggered Snapshot() is then run, after which the same operands are recorded again along with store_emptied (store last index below the snapshot index).

basis.prefix: inmemConfig supplies the timing defaults; TrailingLogs=0 makes compactionWithTrailing delete up to the snapshot index and the large SnapshotThreshold makes the threshold test false for the control. MakeCluster(1, t, conf) starts the real node over InmemTransport with InmemStore for logs and stable state; the test polls r.State() for Leader before applying so the apply is accepted by the leader. The observed transition is produced by the production snapshot path (Raft.Snapshot -> runSnapshots -> takeSnapshot -> compactLogs), not by editing or stubbing production logic; shouldSnapshot and the index accessors are package-internal reads of the runtime object.

scope.description: One process, one real single-node cluster built over the test monotonic log store with default TrailingLogs/SnapshotThreshold and SnapshotInterval shortened to 150ms. The node applies one command, takes an internal snapshot, opens it and raises its index by 100, then runs the production Restore. Store last index, cached snapshot index, applied index, stored-snapshot count and shouldSnapshot are recorded before the restore, immediately after it, and after 700ms (more than four intervals).

basis.prefix: The cluster is created with the snapshot helper's custom constructor using Peers=1, Bootstrap=true and MonotonicLogs=true, so the node's log store is the test monotonic wrapper over InmemStore and IsMonotonic is genuinely true; the same log store is passed to BootstrapCluster. The restore input is produced by the target's own Snapshot() future and Open(), with only meta.Index adjusted upward as the existing restore tests do, so the payload and metadata stay the target's own. No production logic is modified; observations are package-internal reads of the runtime object plus the snapshot store's List().

scope.description: One process, two real raft instances bootstrapped over InmemTransport with TrailingLogs=0 plus a third fresh unbootstrapped instance merged into the same transport set. The leader applies one command, takes a user snapshot (compacting its log), applies a second command, then adds the fresh node with AddVoter and waits up to five seconds for that node's cached snapshot index to become non-zero. The fresh node's log store last index, snapshot index, applied index, commit index, store_emptied and shouldSnapshot are then recorded, together with the leader's prepared snapshot index and the AddVoter result.

basis.prefix: MakeCluster(2, t, conf) with conf.TrailingLogs=0 gives two real Voters over InmemTransport with InmemStore logs and stable state, and waits for a leader; MakeClusterNoBootstrap(1, t, nil) creates the third instance with an empty log and no configuration; Merge plus FullyConnect wire all three transports so the fresh node is reachable. The leader's own snapshot path (Raft.Snapshot -> takeSnapshot -> compactLogs) removes the logs up to the snapshot index, so the fresh node cannot be caught up by log entries alone and the leader must ship a snapshot; the harness waits for the target's snapshot index rather than for a fixed delay so the sample is taken after the install actually happened. No production logic is modified; all observations are package-internal reads of the runtime objects.

scope.description: One process: two real raft instances bootstrapped with TrailingLogs=0 plus a third fresh instance merged into the same transport set. The leader applies an entry, takes a snapshot, applies another, then adds the fresh node with AddVoter and lets it catch up for 500ms. The new voter is then isolated at the transport level, the leader applies three more commands and takes a second snapshot (its own log compacted up to that index), the transport is reconnected, and the harness waits until the isolated node's cached snapshot index reaches the leader's snapshot index before sampling, after a further 150ms, its log store last index, snapshot index, applied index, commit index, store_emptied and shouldSnapshot.

basis.prefix: MakeCluster(2, t, conf) with conf.TrailingLogs=0 supplies the two Voters and the leader; MakeClusterNoBootstrap(1, t, nil) supplies the third instance with an empty log, default trailing count and default threshold, which is the node whose verdict is measured. Merge plus FullyConnect wire the transports; cluster.Disconnect on the third node's address isolates it in both directions and FullyConnect restores it, so the leader cannot reach it while it snapshots and compacts, and after reconnection the leader's replication for that peer must fall back to sending its latest snapshot (the existing replicateTo path that switches to SEND_SNAP when the previous log entry is unavailable). No production logic is modified; the sampling is of the third node's own runtime state, and the wait is on the observed snapshot index rather than a fixed delay.

experiments.revision_reason: The previous construction never left the follower below its snapshot index because AddVoter appended a configuration entry above the installed snapshot and replication kept the log filled. This revision isolates the added voter before taking the leader's snapshot, so after reconnection the follower must install a snapshot at an index above whatever stale log entries it still holds, which is the state the source reading predicts and the previous run could not reach.

experiments.revision_reason: The previous construction never left the follower below its snapshot index because AddVoter appended a configuration entry above the installed snapshot and replication kept the log filled. This revision isolates the added voter before taking the leader's snapshot, so after reconnection the follower must install a snapshot at an index above whatever stale log entries it still holds, which is the state the source reading predicts and the previous run could not reach.

scope.description: One process, one real single-node cluster with TrailingLogs=0, SnapshotThreshold=10000 and SnapshotInterval=1h. After the node becomes leader one command is applied and a user Snapshot() is run, then store last index, snapshot index, applied index, stored-snapshot count and shouldSnapshot are recorded. The production takeSnapshot is then invoked twice, and after each invocation the same operands are recorded together with the returned snapshot-id presence and any error.

basis.prefix: inmemConfig supplies the defaults; TrailingLogs=0 makes the compaction triggered by the user snapshot trim up to the snapshot index and the large threshold makes the control verdict false before that. MakeCluster(1, t, conf) starts the real node over InmemTransport with InmemStore for logs and stable state; the test waits for Leader before applying so the apply is accepted. takeSnapshot is the package-internal production routine that runSnapshots calls on its own timer, so invoking it directly removes the wait on SnapshotInterval while still exercising the production snapshot, compaction and configuration-read paths and the FSM's Snapshot call; no production logic is modified and all operands are package-internal reads of the runtime object plus the snapshot store's List().
